description:
`lib/POSIX.pm` (s492c member 2) defines its own errno constants as literal
numbers -- THIS MACHINE's numbers:

    sub EAGAIN () { 11 }   sub ENOSYS () { 38 }
    sub EWOULDBLOCK () { 11 }   sub ENOTEMPTY () { 39 }   ... (32 names, lines 119-130)

`lib/Errno.pm` ALREADY carries the same table, generated from the real Errno
on the build machine (its own header says "Regenerate if the platform errno
set changes").  So there are TWO readings of one platform fact, and they will
drift the first time either is regenerated -- rule 11's smell, with a
portability edge on it.

WHERE THEY DISAGREE ON macOS (errno 1-34 are the historical V7 numbering and
match; from there they do not):

    name          Linux   macOS/BSD
    EAGAIN          11       35
    EWOULDBLOCK     11       35
    EDEADLK         35       11
    ENOTEMPTY       39       66
    ENOSYS          38       78

A program that does `use POSIX; ... if ($! == EAGAIN)` would therefore be
WRONG on macOS -- silently, which is the bad kind.  Nothing in PCL's own suite
sees it, because the suite runs on Linux; the install matrix is where it would
show.

FIX (small, and it removes 12 lines): POSIX's errno constants become one-line
forwards to Errno's -- `sub EAGAIN () { Errno::EAGAIN() }` -- so the platform
numbers live in exactly one file, the one whose header already says how it is
regenerated.  Errno.pm spells them `use constant NAME => N;`, so they are
callable as `Errno::NAME()`.  Check while there whether any OTHER constant in
lib/POSIX.pm is a platform fact rather than a C-standard one (the limits and
float families are standard; `int_frac_digits => 127` is CHAR_MAX, which is
also a platform fact but the same on both).

Found by s495's platform-symbol audit of the s492c batch (the install matrix
needs the list).  NOT a regression: the numbers are right on the machine PCL
is developed and tested on.
subject: lib/POSIX.pm hardcodes THIS MACHINE's errno numbers, a second copy of lib/Errno.pm's table -- 5 of them differ on macOS
